purpose: Consolidate legacy stage-centric documentation into current owner-based authorities without creating a second archive hierarchy in the active source tree.
source_classes_pending_consolidation: docs/foundation historical STAGE_* task contracts, validation reports, audits and baselines
stage-specific records under provider, UI, catalog, discovery and operations documentation

target_owners.live_volatile_state: Git and GitHub resolved by ./songchart ai status --json
target_owners.durable_rules: current project/module machine and Markdown authorities
target_owners.exact_historical_evidence: Git commit, pull-request and release history

conversion_rules: Do not move every legacy stage document into a new archive folder; that only relocates duplication.
Extract durable rules and decisions into their current semantic owner before deleting a legacy source.
Extract accepted chronology into DEVELOPMENT_HISTORY without preserving obsolete operational instructions as active guidance.
Promote repeated guarded failures into regression-ledger.json and reusable but unguarded lessons into AI_LEARNING_LEDGER.md.
Use Git/PR history as the exact immutable copy of retired stage evidence unless legal, compliance or release evidence requires an explicit retained document.
A historical file may be deleted only after active links, tests, verifiers, generators and documentation consumers no longer require its path.
Compatibility pointers are permitted only when they route to one current owner and do not duplicate content.
Historical stage documents are migration inputs, not AI orientation sources; AI must use current authorities first.

allowed_when: unique legal or compliance evidence cannot be represented by current authority plus Git history
release evidence is required by an active release contract
an external immutable reference requires the historical path
retention_exception.requirement: Retained historical files must declare why Git history plus structured owners are insufficient.

migration_sequence: inventory legacy stage files and all active consumers
classify each file by durable information owner
delete redundant historical files in bounded batches
